title: Best Places to Celebrate Diwali 2026 in India
summary: Five cities where Diwali 2026 looks completely different. Ayodhya Deepotsav, Amritsar Golden Temple, Jaipur bazaars, Varanasi ghats and Goa Narkasur.
body_markdown:
Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8. The full festive window runs from Dhanteras on Friday, November 6 through Bhai Dooj on Wednesday, November 11. The Sunday date means most people get a three-day weekend without leave, or five to six days with just one day off.


Where you celebrate changes the experience entirely. Ayodhya runs a three-day government event with 33 lakh diyas on the Saryu riverfront. Amritsar celebrates Bandi Chhor Divas, a Sikh observance that lights the Golden Temple for 48 continuous hours. Jaipur turns its walled city bazaars into a lit corridor through a municipal illumination competition. Varanasi offers two separate festivals 16 days apart. Goa has a neighbourhood effigy-building competition found nowhere else in India.


## **How to Choose a Diwali Destination**


The best places to celebrate diwali 2026 depend on what kind of experience you want. Visual spectacle, religious atmosphere, shopping, or a beach-and-festival combination all lead to different cities. The five destinations below are covered by what they specifically offer on this date.


## **Ayodhya: Deepotsav on the Saryu River (November 5 to 7)**


Ayodhya Deepotsav 2026 is the 10th edition of the annual lamp-lighting event. It runs from November 5 to 7, with the main ceremony on the evening of November 7. The administration has planned 33 lakh earthen diyas across Ram Ki Paidi and the Saryu riverfront. The[2025 edition set a Guinness World Record](https://newsonair.gov.in/ayodhya-sets-guinness-world-record-with-25-lakh-diyas-lit-and-1121-vedacharyas-performing-aarti-together/) with 22.23 lakh diyas lit simultaneously.


The lit ghats are pass-controlled. The public watches from Naya Ghat, the Saryu bridge and the downstream ghats. Roads into the ghat zone close from the afternoon. Arrive at your viewing position by early afternoon.


A laser and drone show follows the lamp-lighting. Ram Leela performances and cultural events run across all three days at Ram Katha Park.


Ayodhya is connected by air through the[Maharshi Valmiki International Airport](https://www.aai.aero/en) , by rail to Lucknow, and by road through the Delhi to Lucknow corridor. Accommodation fills completely during Deepotsav week. Many visitors stay in Lucknow, about 135 km away, and travel in for the evening.


## **Amritsar: Bandi Chhor Divas at the Golden Temple**


The Sikh celebration of Bandi Chhor Divas coincides with Diwali. It marks the release of Guru Hargobind from Gwalior Fort along with 52 other prisoners. The Golden Temple is fully illuminated, and the celebration runs continuously for about 48 hours.


The fireworks display over the Sarovar is one of the most photographed moments of any Indian festival. The Harmandir Sahib stays open through the night, and the 2 AM to 5 AM window is the most atmospheric time to visit.


Amritsar in November has comfortable temperatures between 12 and 25 degrees Celsius. The Wagah Border ceremony, Jallianwala Bagh and the old city heritage walk all fit around the Diwali visit.


Book accommodation at least two to three weeks before Diwali. Hotels near the Golden Temple fill first.


## **Jaipur: Illuminated Bazaars and Nahargarh Fort at Night**


Jaipur’s Diwali works at a city scale. The municipal government runs an official illumination competition between the merchant associations of Johari Bazaar, Bapu Bazaar, Tripolia Bazaar and Kishanpole Bazaar. Each competes to produce the most decorated stretch. The result is a continuous lit corridor across the[UNESCO World Heritage-listed walled city](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1605/) .


Nahargarh Fort on the hilltop is lit and visible from the old city streets. Hawa Mahal is fully illuminated. Rooftop restaurants overlooking the old city offer fireworks views.


The shopping is strong during this window. Johari Bazaar for jewellery, Bapu Bazaar for textiles and mojari, and Tripolia Bazaar for brassware and lac bangles all run extended hours.


Jaipur is about 280 km from Delhi, roughly 5 to 6 hours by bus. Check current schedules on the[Jaipur bus booking page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/jaipur-bus-booking-online) .


## **Varanasi: Two Festival Windows in One Month**


Varanasi offers something no other city can: two Diwali-related events 16 days apart. Diwali on November 8 lights the ghats with diyas and enhances the nightly Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat. Dev Deepawali on November 24 turns the entire 84-ghat stretch into a wall of flame with over 11 lakh diyas.


For a single visit, Dev Deepawali on November 24 is the more distinctive event. For a longer trip, plan around both dates and experience the quiet middle period (November 10 to 23) when the ghats belong to the Kartik Snaan devotees and the morning boat rides.


## **Goa: Narkasur Effigies Before Dawn**


Goa’s Diwali tradition is unlike anything in the rest of India. Neighbourhoods compete to build the tallest Narkasur effigy, a towering paper-and-wood construction of the demon Narakasura. The effigies are burned before dawn on Diwali day. The scale and creativity of the constructions in Margao, Ponda and Panaji are worth travelling for.


November is also the start of Goa’s tourist season. Beaches are cleaned after the monsoon, shacks reopen, and water is warm for swimming. Diwali in Goa combines the festival with the start of the beach season.


## **How to Plan Around the Diwali 2026 Calendar**


The Sunday alignment gives most people Saturday November 7 to Monday November 9 without leave. Taking Tuesday November 10 off extends the window to Bhai Dooj on Wednesday November 11.


For Ayodhya, arrive by November 6. For Amritsar, arrive by November 7. For Jaipur and Varanasi, November 7 arrival gives a full day before Diwali night. For Goa, the Narkasur burning happens before dawn on November 8.


***Note:*** Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **When is Diwali 2026?**


Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8, with the full cluster running from Dhanteras on November 6 to Bhai Dooj on November 11.


### **Which city is best for Diwali celebrations in India?**


Ayodhya for the Deepotsav spectacle, Amritsar for the Golden Temple illumination, Jaipur for city-wide lighting, and Goa for the Narkasur tradition.


### **What is Ayodhya Deepotsav?**


Deepotsav is a government-organised lamp-lighting event on the Saryu riverfront, planned with 33 lakh diyas in 2026 across Ram Ki Paidi.


### **What is Bandi Chhor Divas at the Golden Temple?**


Bandi Chhor Divas is the Sikh celebration marking Guru Hargobind’s release from Gwalior Fort, observed with a 48-hour illuminated celebration at the Golden Temple.


### **Is Varanasi good for Diwali?**


Varanasi offers two festival windows: Diwali on November 8 and the more distinctive Dev Deepawali on November 24 with ghats lit from Assi to Rajghat.


### **What is the Narkasur tradition in Goa?**


Neighbourhoods build and burn towering effigies of Narakasura before dawn on Diwali day. It is a tradition specific to Goa with competitive effigy-building across towns.


### **How many days off does Diwali 2026 give?**


The Sunday alignment gives a three-day weekend. Taking one day of leave on Tuesday, November 10 extends it to five or six days.


### **When should I book hotels for Diwali travel?**


Book at least two to three weeks before Diwali. Ayodhya and Amritsar fill earliest because of their specific festival events.


### **Can I visit both Diwali and Dev Deepawali in Varanasi?**


Diwali is November 8 and Dev Deepawali is November 24. Covering both requires a 16-day stay or two separate visits.


### **What is the closest Diwali destination from Delhi?**


Jaipur at 5 to 6 hours by bus is the most accessible. Amritsar and Varanasi are overnight journeys. Ayodhya connects through Lucknow.
